# 'stack restack' with a branch checked out in another worktree
# that conflicts during restack.
# The conflict should be aborted and the user told to restack
# from that worktree.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-02-23T21:00:00Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git add init.txt
git commit -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init

# Create a stack: main -> feature1 -> feature2
# feature1 modifies a separate file (no conflict).
# feature2 modifies init.txt (will conflict with main).

git add feature1.txt
gs bc feature1 -m 'feature1'

cp $WORK/extra/feature2.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
gs bc feature2 -m 'feature2'

# Create a worktree for feature2.
# Must leave feature2 first.
gs bco feature1
git worktree add ../wt-feature2 feature2

# Create a conflicting change on main.
gs bco main
cp $WORK/extra/main-conflict.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
git commit -m 'Conflict on main'

# Restack from feature1.
gs bco feature1
gs stack restack

# feature1 should restack fine.
stderr 'feature1: restacked on main'

# feature2 should conflict, abort, and warn.
stderr 'feature2: conflict while restacking in worktree'
stderr 'feature2: run ''gs branch restack'' from that worktree'

# The other worktree should be clean (rebase aborted).
cd ../wt-feature2
git status --porcelain
stdout '^$'

-- repo/init.txt --
initial content

-- repo/feature1.txt --
feature1 content

-- extra/feature2.txt --
feature2 content

-- extra/main-conflict.txt --
main conflicting content
